source_message.text:
3.3V rail (AXP2101 DCDC1, 2A) — primary power source when power board is connected:
\- ESP32-S3 module
\- INA219
\- All I2C sensors (SCD41, BME280, ENS160) via sensor board
\- I2C display
\- TTP223, AM312 PIR

5V rail (MT3608 boost, 500mA) — controlled by ESP32 GPIO3:
\- SPS30 particulate sensor
\- ZE08-CH2O formaldehyde sensor
\- SK6812 LEDs (if wired to 5V — depends on version)

3.3V rail (ME6211A LDO, 1A) — only active when USB-C on main board connected WITHOUT power board:
\- Same 3.3V rail as above — Schottky diode OR-ing means whichever source is present wins. Used for standalone programming.

Battery (3.7–4.2V) — feeds AXP2101 which then feeds everything above.

Simple rule: in normal operation AXP2101 powers everything. The LDO only kicks in when programming without the power board connected.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Ok, perfect, what do you think about AXP2101, is there an easier way to have this solved, I need to be able to charge battery while the device works and also have 3.3V and 5V rails. If there is a better way to do it and simpler you can suggest something

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: But it must be battery efficient as aim will be to make battery work as long as possible.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: It should work without battery as well I think

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Dusko,

USB is fully working after the rework (U3 removed, data lines
bridged), boards enumerate and flash fine. Here is how the power and
AXP2101 behave after that, tested on both boards with identical
results:

1\. DCDC1 idles at 3.16V. The register is confirmed 3.3V (0x82 reads
0x12), so the converter regulates 4 percent low.
2\. Any load transient collapses the rail: SPI flash erase (about
150mA step) or WiFi TX burst (300-400mA) drops the 3.3V below
2.5V and hard resets the ESP32. Brown-out detector disabled makes
no difference, it is a true rail collapse. Adding 330uF external
capacitance does not help. The board cannot run standalone on USB.
3\. It works when powered from battery only (VSYS around 3.8V), but
fails on 5V USB input. So it fails exactly when the buck actually
has to regulate, and survives near dropout.
4\. Writing DCDC1 to 3.4V over I2C helps a lot: boot, WiFi serving and
a full 1.9MB OTA write all pass. But the WiFi calibration surge at
reboot still collapses it. Also strange: the 0x82 write was
ignored on several boots (readback stayed 0x12) and then latched
on a later boot. Other register writes verify fine, and the VBUS
input current limit default is 1.5A, so it is not input limiting.
5\. I replaced L3 with a larger 2.2uH inductor with much higher
saturation current. No change at all. The inductor is not the
problem, the original DFE252010F spec was fine anyway.
6\. During further testing, DCDC1 on board 2 degraded progressively
and finally died: its output now measures about 265 ohm to GND
with everything disconnected, so the output stage is leaking.
7\. With an external 3.3V feed the whole board works perfectly for
hours: boot, PSRAM, e-paper, WiFi, web UI, sensors. Everything
downstream is healthy.

My conclusion: the AXP2101 chips themselves are suspect (bad batch,
counterfeit, moisture damage at reflow, or parts with non-standard
factory programming). I asked the factory for the sourcing and lot
codes. One thing worth checking on your side: the local input
decoupling on the DCDC1 VIN pins in the layout, whether there is a
capacitor close to the pin or only the bulk group further away.

Do you see any other explanation that fits all of this? Hi Dusko,

execution.observed_behavior: Both tested boards operate from battery, but under 5V USB input the AXP2101 power path cannot sustain load transients, causing rail collapse and preventing standalone USB operation.

routing_warnings.description: The abnormal L3 voltage readings describe DCDC1 output regulation and manufacturing variance rather than the broader source-selection power path.
The concrete failure in this message is native USB enumeration; the successful idle 3.3V observation is only partial evidence for the broader power path.
The detailed low-voltage, transient-collapse, register, and degraded-output observations also support the narrower DCDC1 regulation Requirement.
The freelancer's claim concerns placement of converter decoupling capacitors, not verification of the complete AXP2101 power path.
The dead DCDC1 output and use of an external 3.3V supply concern the narrower rail-regulation failure trajectory.
The unsuccessful AXP2101 replacement attempt is evidence of persistence in the DCDC1 failure investigation, with uncertain soldering quality.
